_comment: Ambient air quality standards a station reading is measured against, one table
per ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country, plus WHO for a country with none. See
standards.py for the rules; the short version:
EVERY VALUE IS µg/m³, CO INCLUDED. Where the source writes mg/m³ or ppm, the
value here is converted and `note` says from what.
One number per pollutant: the 24-hour limit where the standard sets one, else
Adding a country is an edit here, never a change to Python.

ZA.name: National Ambient Air Quality Standards (South Africa)
ZA.phrase: the South African standard (NAAQS, GN 1210 of 2009 and GN 486 of 2012)
ZA.source: GN 1210 of 24 December 2009 (Government Gazette 32816), https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/328161210.pdf, and GN 486 of 29 June 2012 (Government Gazette 35463) for PM2.5, https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/35463gon486.pdf, both under section 9(1) of the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004

pm25.note: in force 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2029; 25 from 1 January 2030

BR.name: Padrões de qualidade do ar (Brazil)
BR.phrase: the Brazilian standard (CONAMA Resolution 506 of 2024, interim stage PI-2)
BR.source: CONAMA Resolução 506 of 5 July 2024, Anexo I, interim standard PI-2 in force from 1 January 2025, https://conama.mma.gov.br/?option=com_sisconama&task=arquivo.download&id=827

no2.note: highest hourly mean of the day; the resolution sets no 24-hour limit

o3.note: highest moving 8-hour average of the day

co.note: 9 ppm in the resolution, converted at its reference conditions of 25 °C and 760 mmHg

WHO.name: WHO global air quality guidelines (2021)
WHO.phrase: the WHO 2021 guideline (no national standard is configured for this country)
WHO.source: World Health Organization, WHO global air quality guidelines, 2021, https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240034228
